cf.title: psql: Don't offer USING INDEX after REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) or (ANALYZE)

input.subject: psql: Don't offer USING INDEX after REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) or (ANALYZE)

verdict_reasoning: The problem is stated with the two failing commands and their error messages, and the cost stays inside psql tab completion. One fixable design objection survived, maintenance-fit-1: psql would carry its own copy of a server rule about REPACK options, and nothing ties the two together. That is a judgment for a committer who knows tab-complete.in.c, together with the back-patch question. Only one message is visible and the code was not read.

brief.title: psql: skip USING INDEX completion after REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) or (ANALYZE)
brief.problem: psql tab completion after a REPACK option list offers USING INDEX even when CONCURRENTLY or ANALYZE is enabled. Without a table name, REPACK USING INDEX processes every eligible table, which neither option allows, so the suggested command always fails. This affects psql users on master and REL_19_STABLE.
brief.proposed_design: psql reads the completed REPACK option list and leaves out USING INDEX when CONCURRENTLY or ANALYZE (or ANALYSE) ends up enabled, with the last setting of an option winning as on the server. The reader only interprets plain unquoted option names and values. For quoted names or values, signed numbers or other forms, psql keeps today's completions.
user_visible_surface: psql tab completion after REPACK (option list) no longer offers USING INDEX when CONCURRENTLY or ANALYZE is enabled.
author_claims: REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) USING INDEX and REPACK (ANALYZE) USING INDEX without a table name always fail, so the suggestion is never useful.
USING INDEX is still offered with no options, with VERBOSE, with both options off, and after an explicit table name.
Handling quoted names, quoted values and signed numbers took about 80 more lines, which the author judged not worth it.
New 010_tab_completion.pl cases fail without the fix, and all psql TAP tests pass on master and REL_19_STABLE with GNU readline.
The patch applies to REL_19_STABLE; older branches lack REPACK and are not affected.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. No one has replied, and back-patching to REL_19_STABLE and the choice of the simple or the 80-line parser are open.
unclear: The author has not tested with libedit.
The material does not say whether other REPACK options or option combinations have similar completions that always fail.
The material does not say how the option list reader handles a value-less option followed by an unknown option name.

objections.title: Tab completion copies a server-side semantic rule that can drift
objections.failure_scenario: A later release lets REPACK (ANALYZE) or (CONCURRENTLY) run over all tables with a clustering index. The developer changes the server check and the docs but not tab-complete.in.c. psql keeps hiding USING INDEX for a valid command, no test fails, and users find out only when they notice the completion is missing.
objections.argument: Most psql completion follows the grammar, but this patch encodes a rule from the server's execution checks: which options forbid the no-table form. Message #1 adds its own reader for the option list, with last-setting-wins semantics, so psql now has a second copy of option evaluation that has to match the server. Nothing ties the two copies together. A newer psql connected to an older server, or the reverse, has no server-version check that would show the rule is per release.
objections.author_must_show: What would make a later change to the server's REPACK option rules also update or break this completion, and how should psql handle servers of a different major version?

critic.reasoning: The patch adds an option-list reader with last-setting-wins rules that copies a server execution check, and the new tests would not catch a server change. The cross-version part has no case today because REPACK is new in 19, and the drift only hides a suggestion.

touch_points.reason: psql stops offering USING INDEX after a REPACK option list that enables CONCURRENTLY or ANALYZE.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: tab-complete.in.c gains a REPACK option list reader that must keep matching the server's option rules.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: If a later release relaxes the server's REPACK option rules, what would make this completion get updated or make a test fail?
Does any other code in tab-complete.in.c already evaluate option values, or is this option list reader the first of its kind there?
What does the option list reader do when a value-less option is followed by an unknown option name?
Do the new 010_tab_completion.pl cases pass when psql is built with libedit?
Do other REPACK options or option combinations also lead to a completion that always fails?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows psql tab completion (tab-complete.in.c) and the REPACK option rules would have to own it. No one has replied to message #1.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a small psql-side reader of the REPACK option list that must match the server's rules for as long as REPACK keeps them. If the two drift, psql hides a valid suggestion and the command itself still works.
committability.author_follow_up: Message #1 offers to post the 80-line version that handles quoted names and values if reviewers prefer it. No other sign.

priority.reason: The 7.1 KB patch touches only tab-complete.in.c and its TAP test and helps psql users who type REPACK with these options. The one surviving objection is fixable, and its worst case is a missing suggestion.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the reader's handling of unusual option lists and its fit with the existing completion rules are unchecked. The libedit behaviour is untested by the author.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: Add tab-complete for optional view parameters
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql tab completion for the optional view parameters (check_option, security_barrier, security_invoker) in CREATE VIEW ... WITH ( and in ALTER VIEW ... SET/RESET (. A later version also completes the values of check_option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers found that "alter view <name> set<tab>" does not complete to "SET (", because the "SET SCHEMA" and "SET (" choices share the prefix "SET " and no branch handles it. Dean Rasheed also objected to offering check_option in CREATE VIEW, since it steers users away from the SQL-standard WITH CHECK OPTION syntax. The author did not post a new version after the January review, and the entry was closed as stale.
matched_queries: psql tab completion option list parsing
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: set schema" and "set (" alternatives are competing, while completion of the common part "set<space>" leads to a string composition which does not have the check branch (Matches("ALTER", "VIEW", MatchAny, "SET")).

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab-completion refactoring and word-removal feature (was IF-NOT_EXISTS for tab-completion)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set refactors psql_completion by moving the macros to a new header and turning the long else-if chain into standalone ifs in a separate function. On top of that it adds word-shift and word-removal macros, keyword case that follows input, and suggestions for IF (NOT) EXISTS, OR REPLACE and other syntax.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers judged the refactoring too large and not worth the trouble so soon after the 9.6 rewrite of tab completion; Tom Lane's objection about back-patching appears only in quoted lines. Michael Paquier proposed a localized way to add IF (NOT) EXISTS through words_after_create. The author said removing the else chain is the core of the patch, so a localized patch means abandoning it, and the entry was returned with feedback.
matched_queries: psql tab completion option list parsing
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The general consensus seems to be that this feature is too large
a rewrite of tab completion considering a major rewrite was done for 9.6.

precedents_retrieved.title: improve tab-completion behavior when parse text in single quote
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changed psql tab completion so that word-break characters such as "=" inside a single-quoted string do not split it into words. This would let CREATE SUBSCRIPTION ... CONNECTION 'host=... port=...' complete PUBLICATION.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that treating single-quoted strings as one word would rule out tab completion inside strings and could break existing uses, and he proposed fixing the CREATE SUBSCRIPTION completion rules instead. The author posted a V3 along those lines, and Kyotaro Horiguchi posted a WIP using psqlscan.l, but TAP tests still had problems. Michael Paquier returned the entry because the patch was failing under the CF bot and had not been updated for two months.
matched_queries: psql tab completion option list parsing
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So now I think that this approach should be rejected, and that the
right thing is to fix the CREATE SUBSCRIPTION completion rules
to allow more than one "word" between CONNECTION and PUBLICATION.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab completion for SELECT in psql
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql tab completion after SELECT, suggesting column names from all visible tables and function names. Functions that are unlikely to be called directly are filtered out, and later versions use per-server-version queries and add completion after commas.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas found the completions both too broad and too narrow: system catalog columns flood short prefixes, the FROM clause is ignored, and system columns appear inconsistently. He held that the completion must be smarter to be acceptable. He also reported that the query on pg_attribute took about 1 second on a database with a 1000-partition table. An earlier review by Peter Eisentraut found broken older-version queries and an unsettled function filter. The rebased patch of 2018-09-22 got no visible reply before the entry was returned.
matched_queries: psql tab completion option list parsing
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think the completion needs to be smarter to be acceptable.

precedents_retrieved.title: tab-completion debug print
precedents_retrieved.summary: Instrument psql's tab-complete.c so that each completion prints the source line number that produced it, and later the completion text, to stderr. The first version was a compile-time option (TABCOMPLETION_DEBUG); a later version made it a run-time psql option, -g.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut and Tom Lane objected to the run-time option. They said it should not use a short option letter, and that it is a development aid that should stay out of production builds. Peter Eisentraut also asked for evidence of tab completion problems in production that would need it. Michael Paquier closed it as returned with feedback, citing a suggestion of Tom's from a message not shown here.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This is a development option,
not a production option.  I don't think it should be in production
builds at all, let alone be invokable via a simple command-line switch.

precedents_retrieved.title: remove VersionedQuery support from psql tab completion
precedents_retrieved.summary: Remove the VersionedQuery infrastructure from psql tab completion, because it served only publications and subscriptions. After psql's minimum supported server version was raised to v10, nothing used it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that future catalog changes may again affect tab completion. SchemaQuery, the alternative, is harder to use. Nathan Bossart replied that he was fine with leaving the code in place, and the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Do you think we'll never again
make any catalog changes that affect tab completion?

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: add tab completion for \df slash command suffixes
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql tab completion for the \df suffixes \dfa, \dfn, \dfp, \dft and \dfw. It applies to master back to 9.6, with separate patches for 9.5 and 9.4.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Kuntal Ghosh found that the back-branch patches offer \dfp, which exists only from Pg11, and asked for it to be removed. The author agreed to resubmit but did not send a new version before the commitfest ended, despite a reminder from Michael Paquier.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix psql-completion for CREATE INDEX
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes several psql tab-completion bugs: a wrong word position in ALL IN TABLESPACE OWNED BY, the misplaced CONCURRENTLY in CREATE INDEX, and a missing NULL in the SECURITY LABEL list. Later versions add IF NOT EXISTS completion for CREATE INDEX and fix DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY, with an optional multilevel matching variant.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The parts were fixed or committed separately, so nothing was left to apply. The CREATE INDEX fix was done in another thread, and Peter Eisentraut committed a reduced DROP INDEX patch without IF NOT EXISTS, because psql has no IF NOT EXISTS completion elsewhere. The author confirmed the commit and said he would post IF (NOT) EXISTS support as a separate patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I agree that we could use completion support for DROP INDEX
CONCURRENTLY, but I would rather not throw IF NOT EXISTS into the same
patch.  We don't have support for IF NOT EXISTS anywhere else.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert analyze support for partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert analyze support for partitioned tables
Reverted commit(s): Describe (auto-)analyze behavior for partitioned tables; Set pg_class.reltuples for partitioned tables; Document ANALYZE storage parameters for partitioned tables; autovacuum: handle analyze for partitioned tables; Don't reset relhasindex for partitioned tables on ANALYZE
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts the following commits:
1b5617eb844cd2470a334c1d2eec66cf9b39c41a Describe (auto-)analyze behavior for partitioned tables
0e69f705cc1a3df273b38c9883fb5765991e04fe Set pg_class.reltuples for partitioned tables
41badeaba8beee7648ebe7923a41c04f1f3cb302 Document ANALYZE storage parameters for partitioned tables
0827e8af70f4653ba17ed773f123a60eadd9f9c9 autovacuum: handle analyze for partitioned tables

There are efficiency issues in this code when handling databases with
large numbers of partitions, and it doesn't look like there isn't any
trivial way to handle those.  There are some other issues as well.  It's
now too late in the cycle for nontrivial fixes, so we'll have to let
Postgres 14 users continue to manually deal with ANALYZE their
partitioned tables, and hopefully we can fix the issues for Postgres 15.

I kept [most of] be280cdad298 ("Don't reset relhasindex for partitioned
tables on ANALYZE") because while we added it due to 0827e8af70f4, it is
a good bugfix in its own right, since it affects manual analyze as well
as autovacuum-induced analyze, and there's no reason to revert it.

I retained the addition of relkind 'p' to tables included by
pg_stat_user_tables, because reverting that would require a catversion
bump.
Also, in pg14 only, I keep a struct member that was added to
PgStat_TabStatEntry to avoid breaking compatibility with existing stat
files.

Backpatch to 14.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P3] changed how psql splits words inside single-quoted strings, which is a different idea, and its recorded reason does not apply here: this patch changes no word splitting and keeps today's completions when the option list contains quoted text. Message #1 cites only a related committed fix for ON/OFF completion in the REPACK option list, not an earlier rejected attempt.

From the standards and compatibility angle there is nothing to object to. The patch adds no syntax, keyword, GUC or catalog state, nothing pg_dump must round-trip, and no change to what clients see. The only visible change is that psql stops suggesting USING INDEX after REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) or (ANALYZE), where the server rejects it. One point other angles could weigh: psql completion now copies a server rule and should follow the server if that rule is relaxed. That is not a compatibility failure today.

The patch changes only psql tab completion and its TAP test. It touches no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or server ABI, so this angle has nothing to object to. Back-patching to REL_19_STABLE carries no ABI risk because the change is client-side only.

The patch changes only which words psql tab completion offers after a REPACK option list. It adds no privilege, exposure or denial-of-service path, since completion runs on the client and the server still checks the command.

Beyond the drift risk, the cost falls only on psql tab completion users. The patch has no hot-path, catalog or API impact, and it is small. [P3] concerns word splitting inside quoted strings and does not apply here.

No existing Postgres feature, contrib module or extension filters psql tab completion of REPACK USING INDEX by option values, and this kind of fix can only live in tab-complete.in.c. The proposal adds no new mechanism: it narrows an existing completion rule. [P3] concerns word-break handling inside quoted strings and does not apply here.

No demand objection. This fixes a tab completion that always suggests a failing command, every psql user typing REPACK with these options can hit it, and the cost stays inside tab-complete.in.c. Whether a general option-list reader is worth adding for one suggestion is a maintainability question for other angles. [P3] concerns quoted-string word splitting and does not apply.
